checks: Twice the first margin plus the second and third margins is zero. The normals span and have this positive relation, so the three closed halfplanes cover the plane.

The first cap misses the rectangle. On a horizontal edge exactly one remaining cap contains every point. At x=-c the last two overlap on [-c,c] and together cover the full vertical edge. Thus W is 3/10 on horizontal edges and 3/10 plus 3/10 times the central interval indicator on vertical edges.

For every nonnegative convex edge restriction, its even symmetrization is convex and nondecreasing on [0,3]. The average on [0,c] is at most the full half-edge average. This proves the sharp central integral bound even when the edge restriction vanishes.

The two exact vertical bounds are (3/10)(1+9/30)=39/100 and (3/10)(1+11/30)=41/100<4/9. Nonnegative edge integrals combine the bounds. A continuous function of the normal alone can be one on the left outward normal and zero on the other three. It gives a positive denominator and attains 41/100.

overlap.comparison: The roof realization describes a class of admissible normal-dependent convex potentials. It gives no value for the sharp weighted ratio in this specific ordinary rectangle and positive circuit.

readability: The quantified supremum is over a single ordinary rectangle and the given fixed cap profile.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Convex edge restrictions give an exact upper bound of 41/100, attained by a normal multiplier supported on the left edge.
